Petroleo Brasileiro SA Appoints New Executive Director Amid Strategic Growth Plans

Petroleo Brasileiro SA, a leading force in Brazil’s energy sector, has announced the appointment of Ana Paula Mendes as its new Executive Director of Exploration and Production. The decision, revealed by the company’s board on Monday, comes as Petrobras—commonly known as Petroleo Brasileiro SA—continues to advance strategic projects in both pre-salt and post-salt oil reserves.

Mendes, an engineer with over 25 years of experience in the oil and gas industry, will assume her new responsibilities effective July 1. She previously held senior technical and managerial roles at industry leaders, most recently serving as Chief Operating Officer at RioEnergia Ltda. Her appointment is widely seen as a move to reinforce Petrobras’ commitment to technological innovation and operational efficiency.

In a statement, Petrobras CEO Luiz Carvalho said, “Ana Paula Mendes brings a wealth of expertise and a results-driven approach that aligns perfectly with our growth strategy. We are confident that her leadership will enhance our exploration and production capabilities, supporting Brazil’s position as a global energy supplier.”

Petrobras is currently in the midst of expanding its production capacity in the Santos and Campos Basins, with a capital expenditure plan exceeding R$ 64 billion over the next four years. The company’s pre-salt fields have been central to Brazil’s emergence as a major oil exporter, and Mendes’ technical background is expected to be instrumental in further tapping these resources.

Industry observers welcomed the appointment. “Petrobras is at a pivotal moment, with ambitious targets for increasing output and reducing emissions,” said Mariana Rocha, a senior analyst at the Brazilian Institute for Energy Studies. “Mendes has a proven track record in managing complex upstream operations and her expertise will be a valuable asset for the company’s ongoing projects.”

Union representatives also expressed optimism about the new leadership. Paulo Nogueira, spokesperson for the Federation of Oil Workers, commented, “We look forward to working collaboratively with Ms. Mendes to ensure that safety and sustainability remain top priorities as Petrobras advances its exploration activities.”

Mendes herself addressed employees in an internal memo, stating, “I am honored to join Petrobras at such an exciting time. Together, we will pursue our vision for responsible growth and operational excellence, delivering value for our stakeholders and for Brazil.”

Petrobras shares closed up 1.8% on the B3 exchange following the announcement, reflecting positive sentiment from investors regarding the leadership transition.
